subject: Day 13: growth spurt likely tomorrow; lock in EPDS for next week
bodyText:
Today's focus
Day 13. Last day of week 2. The first common growth spurt is likely to start tomorrow or in the next several days — expect 24-48 hours of unusually frequent feeding and fussiness, then a reset. The EPDS (Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale) screen for the mother is due this week or next.

Action items
- Take or schedule the EPDS screen for Anoushka. A score above 10 warrants a call to her OB or PCP; a score of 13 or higher traditionally distinguishes likely depression. ACOG Committee Opinion 757 on perinatal depression screening: https://www.acog.org/clinical/clinical-guidance/committee-opinion/articles/2018/11/screening-for-perinatal-depression
- Brace for the growth spurt: stock easy meals, fully charge breast pump if pumping, hydrate.
- If 529 plan is not yet open, do it today. Front-loading the early years compounds maximally. 529 plan overview on Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/529_plan
- Update emergency contacts on Avi's pediatrician portal. Make sure a second adult can pick him up if you both cannot.
- Continue the feeding log; it ends at the 1-month visit unless the pediatrician asks for more.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Cord stump detached or detaching. Cluster feeding 60-90 minutes most evenings. Mother's lochia alba (minimal yellow-white) or stopping.
- [low concern] Avi sleeping in 60-120 minute increments at night.
- [monitor] Persistent baby blues in Anoushka beyond week 2. 50-80% of mothers experience baby blues; resolution by 2 weeks is typical. Persistence escalates concern toward postpartum depression. Postpartum Support International: https://www.postpartum.net/
- [call within 24h] Yellow tinge still present below the chest. Persistent inability to latch. Fewer than six wet diapers per day. Mother's bleeding suddenly heavier or new pelvic pain.
- [call now] Rectal temperature at or above 100.4F (38.0C) in an infant under 90 days. Lethargy, refusing all feeds, blue or grey color, breathing faster than 60 per minute at rest, persistent grunting, projectile or bilious-green vomiting. Maternal chest pain, severe headache, vision changes, or pad-per-hour bleeding — call OB or 911. Call 911 for blue lips or unresponsiveness!

Enrichment opportunity
Narrate one ordinary task in detail during Avi's next awake-alert window. Conversational turns (not raw word count) predict later language outcomes. Romeo et al. (Psych Science 2018) on PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/

Upcoming
- Day 14-21: first common growth spurt.
- Day 28-35: 1-month well visit window opens; first social smiles begin.
- Day 35-42: peak of the PURPLE crying curve at about 6 weeks corrected age.
- Day 42: maternal 6-week postpartum visit (clearance for exercise and intimacy).

Further reading
- ACOG on screening for perinatal depression: https://www.acog.org/clinical/clinical-guidance/committee-opinion/articles/2018/11/screening-for-perinatal-depression
- Postpartum Support International — screening and hotline: https://www.postpartum.net/
- AAP HealthyChildren overview of the first month: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/default.aspx
- 529 plan overview on Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/529_plan
